items.quote: In the first 11 months of this fiscal, which is April 1 to 1st March 2026, we have commissioned about 1.3 GW of capacity. You know, 1,300 MW of energy sales capacity has been commissioned in the first 11 months of this fiscal, which is 85% solar and 15% wind.

items.statement: Contracted RE power sales capacity grew 3x to 5.7 GW as of 1st March 2026
items.quote: Overall we are a leader in India's C&I segment. We have 5,700 MW or 5.7 GW of contracted, where we have power purchase agreements in place of what is called RE power sales capacity where we are going to sell the energy.

items.statement: 2.7 GW of contracted RE power sales capacity under execution as of 1st March 2026
items.quote: Firstly we have about 2.7 GW of RE power sales capacity which is contracted as of 1st March and is under execution.

items.statement: RE Power Sales EBITDA margin improved from 81% to 83% in 9M FY26
items.quote: So RE power sales segment the EBITDA margins have grown from 81% to 83% and RE services segment also the EBITDA margins have grown from 15% to 22%.

items.statement: Post-ALCM solar tariffs increased 7-10% by state
items.quote: I think the numbers vary a little bit by state but 7% to 10%.

items.statement: Weighted average interest rate fell from 9.2% at start of fiscal to 8.7% as of Dec 2025
items.quote: Second is our weighted average interest rates have fallen from 9.2% at the start of the fiscal to about 8.7% as of Dec '25.

items.statement: Net debt breakdown as of 31st Dec 2025: INR 4,688 Cr operational >1yr, INR 1,781 Cr commissioned this year, INR 1,739 Cr under-construction, INR 1,490 Cr corporate
items.quote: So if you look at the lower half of the page as of 31st December 25 balance sheet, about INR 4,688 crores of net debt is for projects which are operational for greater than a year. Another I NR 1,781 crores is for projects which essentially commissioned during the financial year. Another INR 1,739 crores of debt is for under -construction assets, which have not had any corresponding EBITDA. And ab

items.statement: Data & AI customers represent 42% of 5.7 GW contracted capacity (2.4 GW), grew 10x in <2 years
items.quote: Data and AI continues to be a big growth driver for us. It's 42% of our contracted capacity and interestingly this number has risen nearly 10 times, 10x growth in slightly less than two financial years from 31st March 2024 to about 1st March 2026.

items.statement: 97% of contracted MWs with A-rated or above counterparties (83% AA/AAA/MNC, 14% A-rated)
items.quote: So about 83% of the MWs contracted are with AA, AAA, or multinationals, 14% is with A rated, so about 97% of our volumes are with A rated or above.

items.statement: Contracted portfolio mix 70% solar, 30% wind across 6.5 GW total contracted capacity
items.quote: The total portfolio of contracted capacity is about 6.5 GW and the mix overall remains at 70% solar and 30% wind.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month capacity commissioned reached 1.3 GW as of 1st March 2026, up from ~500 MW at start of FY26
items.quote: So that number as of 1st March 2026 stood at about 1.3 GW of capacity commissioned in the trailing 12 months. And as you can see, this has consistently risen from about nearly 500 MW at the start of the financial year was our trailing 12 months capacity addition to about as of 31st December it's risen to 1.1 GW and now it's 1.3 GW.

items.statement: Grid uptime across entire system remains above 99%
items.quote: For across our entire system the grid uptime remains very high at above 99%.

items.statement: Osaka Gas invested INR 176 Cr for 49% stake in JV in Q3 FY26; JV targets 400+ MW over 3 years
items.quote: And we have already received in the third quarter of FY26 equity contribution of INR 176 crores from Osaka Gas for their 49% stake. And this does also add strategic value to us. It gives us access to JBIC development finance, expands reach with global capital, and makes us more equity efficient in how we do our business.

items.statement: Force majeure protection in PPAs if grid fails to connect; no liquidated damages exposure
items.quote: But for almost all our contracts, right, if the grid does not connect, we would be able to declare that as a force majeure and not be subject to L iquidated Damages (LDs

items.statement: Regulatory changes (cross subsidy surcharge removal, banking norms) pose max 1.5% EBITDA risk on 3 GW operational capacity
items.quote: We've run all of those analysis Mihir and estimated that even if all of those events were to occur, then the maximum EBITDA risk to CleanMax on the 3 GW of contracted capacity is about 1 .5% of our EBITDA.

items.statement: Receivable days remain at very manageable levels
items.quote: The receivable days continue to be at a very manageable number.

items.statement: Bikaner 525 MW CTU plant facing transmission bottlenecks; CTU estimates resolution Oct-Dec 2026
items.quote: The Bikaner 2 connectivity status update that we have from CTU and their estimate is that - the grid itself is connected, the substation is connected, but there are transmission bottleneck more north of the substation which are causing some backdown issues. They estimate that somewhere in the quarter between October to December 2026 is by when they expect to resolve the same.

items.statement: No project-wise or technology-wise capex guidance given for FY27
items.quote: We haven't given that project -wise and technology -wise guidance right now. Let's examine if we provide that.

items.statement: No guidance provided for FY28 capacity additions; only 1-year forward guidance given
items.quote: So we are not giving any guidance for FY 28, Shaunak, because in our business it's pragmatic to only give a guidance for 1 year forward at a time is what we felt because there are a lot of contracting, so many other moving parts in project execution.

items.statement: FY27 capacity addition: ~500 MW CTU wind in Karnataka, ~1 GW non-CTU across Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu plus Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand
items.quote: And yes out of that maybe 0.5 GW is CTU connected wind project which we are building in the state of Karnataka. Puneet Gulati: Yes. Kuldeep Jain: Then the remainder is 1 GW of RE power sales capacity which is really for non -CTU and the four biggest states for us, Puneet, are really Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Tamil

items.statement: Firm evacuation capacity of 3.1 GW uncontracted + 1.6 GW applied for = 4.7 GW evacuation pipeline as of 1st March 2026
items.quote: So firm evacuation that we already possess which is yet to be contracted with customers, right, I'll again repeat, the firm evacuation which is yet to be contracted with customers stands at 3.1 GW for us as of 1st March 2026. And evacuation applied for, which we've not yet been given on a firm basis, is about 1.6 GW.

items.statement: No QIB planned; well equity funded for 3+ years of high growth with strategic partnerships
items.quote: We have no intention of a QIB to answer that very specific question and we believe that we should be well funded for continued high growth over the next three years.

items.statement: RE Power Sales EBITDA margin expected to reach 85-86% in 2-3 years from current 83%
items.quote: And I could be slightly wrong, but I think it goes up to 85%, 86% in 2 to 3 years from today.

items.statement: >50 BD executives; sign ~100 new deals/year; 570+ clients
items.quote: We have 570 clients. We have more than 50 BD executives. In a year , we sign about 100 new deals which means at any point there are 200 to 400 conversations and pipeline discussions going on.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% top-line growth next financial year driven by new verticals
items.quote: we see that, okay, at least we would do around a 30-35% growth from... compared to this year. is what we are looking to do for the next financial year.

items.statement: Aims for double-digit growth in coming year after single-digit growth in previous two years
items.quote: In the last 2 years, our numbers in growth have been single-digit, but I mean, in the coming year, we would look at a double-digit. growth percentage.

items.statement: Plans Rs 2-3 crore capex in Q1 next year funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Maybe a CAPEX of another 2-3 crores would be required, but that we can... we can... Manage that.

items.statement: Intends to initiate capex in mid-April and complete in first quarter
items.quote: So, we intend to do the CAPEX in April, to initiate the Capex in April mid, and have the... have the Capex done in the first quarter of the coming year.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization around 75% with 20-25% headroom
items.quote: See, currently, I would say we are utilizing around 75% of our capacity. There is potential to utilize around 20-25% more capacity.

items.statement: After Rs 2-3 crore capex, top-line capacity estimated at Rs 140-150 crore
items.quote: After another 2-3 crores of capex that we are looking to do, I think we should be able to go up to around 140, 150, within the range of 140, 150 as a top line.

items.statement: Waterproof/facade lighting commands higher pricing, better margins and technical specs
items.quote: the pricing of the product is also higher, there is... the margins are also better. And the technical specifications of the product are also much higher than what is being sold in the trade application.

items.statement: BIS certification for lighting tightened; no new approvals for Chinese manufacturers
items.quote: Now, what the government has done is that they have the BIS certification, which was being given to the Chinese manufacturers earlier. Now, no new Chinese manufacturers are being given the BIS certification.

items.statement: Exports indirect via clients to Middle East, Africa, SAARC; exploring direct exports
items.quote: Currently, we're exporting, but not directly. Our clients are buying from us, and they are exporting to other countries. They're exporting to the Middle East, they've been exporting to Africa, they've been exporting to the Safda region.

items.statement: Mainboard migration eligible by September after 3-year listing requirement
items.quote: the company is planning mainboard migration. We would be eligible... in September, because I think there's a 3-year clause, so by September, we will be eligible.

items.statement: Recruited senior talent across development, operations, sales for new verticals
items.quote: We have recruited better people in our team. We have got senior people in our team, from development to operations to sales.

items.statement: Dollar/rupee and crude price volatility affect import costs; passed through after threshold
items.quote: you see that the dollar prices... the dollar has gone up. It affects our imports, the crude has gone up, so it affects the materials that we buy.

items.statement: Implementing SAP, HRMS, PMS and Industry 4.0 automation to reduce labor dependency
items.quote: we're working on implementation of softwares like SAP, We are doing HRMS softwares, PMS softwares, we are trying to integrate, we're trying to work on the Industry 4.0.
